headline_marked: [[Massive 12TB Steam leak]] reveals decades of unreleased games, including Half-Life 2: Episode 3 builds
headline: Massive 12TB Steam leak reveals decades of unreleased games, including Half-Life 2: Episode 3 builds
summary: A 12-13TB archive of old Steam content from 2003-2013 was publicly accessible, revealing unreleased Valve and third-party game builds, not due to a hack but an exposed endpoint.
details: Valve has reportedly suffered its largest data leak to date, with archivists extracting 12-13TB of old game content. This was not a hack but a result of an endpoint to Valve's legacy infrastructure being publicly accessible. The files are still being explored, but key discoveries include an early weapon asset from Half-Life 2 Episode 3 and scrapped Portal 2 concepts.

The archive consists of old Steam content-server data spanning from 2003 to 2013. This period overlaps with Steam's transition from the proprietary Steam2 system, which used NCF and GCF formats, to the standard HTTP file-tree system known as SteamPipe around March 2013. The dump acts as a preserved time capsule of this era.

Among the findings is an entire early build of Left 4 Dead from June 2008. This version features a different HUD, cut voice lines, altered map sections, and unfinished assets recycled from the Terror Strike mod for Counter-Strike: Condition Zero. It offers a rare glimpse into Valve's more active game development phase.

Portal 2 was reportedly hit hardest by the leak, with modders reconstructing a playable beta build from July 2009. This build dates back to the game's "Core Hub" era, a concept later scrapped for a more direct sequel. Early assets from the F-Stop prequel, developed a year prior with camera mechanics, were also discovered.

The Portal 2 beta also features a completely different, more passive GLaDOS with new animations and voice lines. Some scenes use placeholder assets from Team Fortress and Half-Life due to their unfinished state. Perhaps the most exciting find is a 3D weapon model for "Weaponizer," a concept weapon from the canceled Half-Life 2: Episode 3, showing how close it was to development.

Early builds of CS:GO were also found, showcasing a look much closer to Source in its initial development days. These include a more stylized UI and alpha versions of maps. An MP5-Active weapon, early knife models, cut grenade mechanics, and a Riot Shield from Counter-Strike 1.6 were also present in the files.

The archive also contains builds from 2011 that run on Source physics and movement, featuring early Left 4 Dead 2 engine code and prototype CS:GO UI elements. This period marks the birth of CS:GO as a standalone game, as Valve was initially attempting to port Source to home consoles. Extensive upgrades by Hidden Path Entertainment led to the decision for a new Counter-Strike title.

These are just a few highlights from the massive data dump, with archivists expecting to uncover more information in the coming days. Other tidbits include an early beta build of Sonic 4 Episode 2 for PC, hinting at the breadth of content within the archive.
